reason: The commit removes a decoding step it calls unnecessary without establishing that the decoding was incorrect.
The release note introduces iter_lines without making an efficiency claim.
The artwork is added as source comments above the docstring, so it would not appear as part of that docstring in help output.
One conditional gzip-header update is removed, but the diff does not establish that automatic gzip headers were removed throughout the library.
The schedule runs less often, but whether its previous activity was unnecessary is an inference.
The patch adds visible HTML spacing as well as a blank line, contrary to the claim that it makes no user-facing change.
The markup moves the call to action and the stylesheet removes a declaration, but the effect on rendering is not shown.
Removing the Makefile's init target does not eliminate the need to install dependencies somewhere.
The API guide changes an example, while the visible advanced-guide change removes a prose reference rather than replacing an example.
The shown change removes the argument from r.send and forwards the pool into Request instead of removing it from the public helper.
The notes list Content-Type parsing and consistency of header errors as separate fixes without the claimed cause-and-effect relationship.
The general proxy is looked up first, with the scheme proxy used as the fallback.
The file-upload test is truncated before its pickle and send assertions, so only the ordinary request's full round trip is visible.
The conflict test sets cookies using different path arguments, and both set calls occur before the expected exception.
The iteration changes address these sites on Python 3, but the patch cannot establish compatibility for the entire library.
The import and proxy-manager edit are visible, but the claimed streamlining of the configuration logic is not established in the truncated hunk.
The test name's spelling is corrected, but both names already have the test prefix and the text shows no change to whether the suite runs.
The specific method list is replaced in the README, but the visible index text is a general description without that list.
The version numbers are shown, but the claim that the new version was the latest stable release is unverified.
The formatting changes from a cross-reference to bold text, while the claim about readability is subjective.
The file list supports vendoring chardet, but does not establish the separate claim about what users must install to enable detection.
The visible hunks show a fallback for importing poll, but end before any HTTPResponse change that would establish its role in that fallback.
The only change imports poster, with no other evidence tying it to multipart submissions in this commit.
The excerpt shows a single blank-line insertion and does not place it at the end of iter_lines.
The dependency is pinned to 0.0.4, but the text does not label that version stable or establish what the resolver previously selected.
The change removes a CI matrix entry without establishing that Requests dropped Python 3.2 support itself.
The code concatenates the path and query directly, without showing the separator needed to form a path with a query string.
The new curl flag follows redirects, while the remote-filename flag is already present on both sides.
The sponsor link and PayPal form change, but the record does not say the donation interface was obsolete.
The image source changes, but the old link is not shown to be broken and the replacement is not verified.
The new proxy API is shown, but the text does not identify the previous ProxyManager as deprecated.
The commit adds gzip test coverage without itself changing or establishing the correctness of the decompression implementation.
